framing_check_method: grep -niE 'confirm|predicts|fixes|derive[sd]?|cleared|reward|falsif|validat|k3.?x?.?t2|k3xt2' over X1-cmb/run_commands.txt-adjacent prose, X4_RESULT.md, X3-pta/README.md, X2-cosmic-web/REPORT.md, and the four experiment scripts' framing docstrings. Every hit is either a negated/hedged statement ('not a K3xT2 prediction', 'no claim that K3xT2 predicts or fixes...'), a benign use of 'validates'/'confirms' about a numeric cross-check (e.g. CAMB spline validation, OS reimplementation agreement), or an explicit statement that the P1 falsification rule's language ('falsified'/'confirmed') is NOT used. No instance found of M0's outcome being called a K3xT2 prediction/derivation, and none of 'confirms', 'cleared decisively', or 'the data reward' used as an actual claim (only as banned-word examples in the scripts' own commentary).

Ran `prlimit --as=10737418240 -- <venv> x4_bao_cmb_sn.py fit --cut 1580 --model {m0,lcdm,cpl} --start-lo 0 --start-hi 6` (6 of the registered 20 seeded starts, same seed formula default_rng(9000000+i)). Result: m0 chi2=1408.955 (recorded 1408.955, exact), lcdm chi2=1404.2795 (recorded 1404.28), cpl chi2=1397.2808 (recorded 1397.281) -- all three headline chi2_min values reproduced from a fresh clone with 30% of the registered starts. These three are therefore reproduced:false; their headline numbers were instead checked by (a) independent arithmetic recomputation with scipy (see item verdicts below) and (b) direct code reading of the committed scripts against the registered statistic, not by re-executing the heavy simulation.

checklist.text: registered rule applied exactly, every deviation disclosed
checklist.verdict: STANDS for X1, X2, X4; DOES NOT FULLY STAND for X3
checklist.evidence: X1: gate formula, family (sub_b0/sub_b1/sup_b0/sup_b1), Sidak p_corr=1-(1-p_min)^2, and the WMAP-primary/SMICA-conditional-no-pooling structure all match registration.json verbatim (code-read in x1_cmb.py). Disclosed deviations (N_null 500 vs registered up-to-2000; resumable calibration) are recorded in result.json's N_shortfall_vs_registered field and do not touch the algorithm/seeds/formula. X2: G=slice(3,13) (10 bins, [20,60)) and F=bins[0:3] ([8,20)) are disjoint by construction (RS_EDGES = np.arange(8.0,60.01,4.0), code comment 'bins 0..2 = F, 3..12 = G'); Hartlap factor hart=(NF-p-2)/(NF-1) is the standard formula; gate order (power, then calibration, then topology) matches registration's decision_rule text exactly, verified by reading x2_analyze.py line by line. X4: single SN-cut function used for both 1580/1590 (x4_core.py's load_sn/apply one mask before slicing both the mean vector and covariance), CMB values and inverse-covariance copied verbatim from the fetched arXiv:1808.05724 TeX (see item 7), Wilks dof (2 for CPL-vs-Lambda, 1 for M0-vs-Lambda) and 20-seeded-start minimizer match the registered spec; all three disclosed deviations (inactive CPL w0+wa<0 penalty, CAMB-spline r_drag instead of a closed-form formula, a post-hoc source-only assert) are shown to be numerically inert or a documented strengthening, not silent. X3 departs from its own registered statistic in three ways beyond ordinary disclosed slack: (a) the registration names 'the Allen 2023 Variance of the Hellings-Downs correlation formalism' for the pair covariance; a delete-one-pulsar jackknife covariance was substituted instead (confirmed: enterprise_extensions 3.0.3's frequentist/*.py has no such analytic function per the experiment's own grep, and x3_combine.py computes a jackknife, not an Allen-2023 covariance); (b) the registration's calibration_gates.hd_recovery statistic asks for 'the fitted a with c4 fixed at 0' (a 1-parameter HD-only fit); what is reported is a_hat from the joint 2-parameter (a,b) GLS fit, not a separate c4=0-fixed refit; (c) the CURN amplitude (log10_A_CURN) that the whole GLS fit is conditioned on was never fetched/verified against the NANOGrav 15-yr paper -- a free input, not a registered or literature-sourced constant. All three are disclosed in x3_pta_result.json's deviations list and README.md, so nothing is hidden, but 'the registered rule was applied exactly' cannot be said of X3's covariance and hd_recovery statistic -- only of its P4/OS machinery (see item 6).

checklist.text: X1: the spectrum-match gate, per ell band
checklist.evidence: Read audit/reverse_zero_r2/X1-cmb/wmap/gate.json and smica/gate.json directly (not summarized). Both list 10 band_edges (2,3,6,10,16,28,47,79,134,228,385) and 10 corresponding z_bands. threshold=2.8070337683438042 recomputed independently via scipy: norm.isf(0.025/10)=2.8070337683438042 (exact match). WMAP: all 10 |z_bands| <= 0.851 (max at band index 9), well under 2.807 -> passed=true, matches result.json's gate_max_abs_z=0.851. SMICA: all 10 |z_bands| <= ~0.166 similarly under threshold -> passed=true. Both gates checked per band, not just the reported max, and both pass legitimately given the stored per-band data.

checklist.text: X2: the gate's power (rejects xi=0), the gate range disjoint from the bias-fit range, and the redshift-space treatment
checklist.evidence: Power: x2_results.json reports poisson_reject_rate=0.995 (95% CI [0.972,0.9999]) and x3_reject_rate=0.985 (95% CI [0.957,0.997]) against the fiducial 95th-percentile threshold, both >=0.95 with margin, power_pass=true -- read directly from x2_analyze.py's own computation (binomtest exact CIs), not just the summary numbers. Disjoint ranges: x2_lib.py line 29, RS_EDGES=np.arange(8.0,60.01,4.0) with an inline comment '0..2 = F [8,20), 3..12 = G [20,60)'; x2_fit_bias.py fits only xi_d[:3] (F); x2_analyze.py's gate uses G=slice(3,13) (10 bins) exclusively -- the two ranges share no bin index. Redshift-space treatment: x2_lib.py line 344, vlos = f*(displacement . line_of_sight) + Normal(0, SIGV=4), i.e. linear Kaiser RSD along the radial line of sight plus a sigma_v=4 Mpc/h Gaussian FoG term, matching the registered null_model text exactly.

checklist.text: X3: the optimal-statistic normalisation, the pair covariance, and the P4-term definition against param_loop_sim.py
checklist.verdict: PARTIAL: OS normalization and P4 definition STAND; pair covariance DOES NOT STAND as registered (see item 3c)
checklist.evidence: OS normalization: x3_verify_os_result.json cross-checks the repo's numpy pairwise-OS reimplementation against enterprise_extensions.OptimalStatistic.compute_os on a 3-pulsar subset; xi, rho and sig arrays are bit-identical (max_abs_diff_xi=0.0, max_rel_diff_rho=0.0, max_rel_diff_sig=0.0), and no_param_not_set_warnings=true rules out a silent PINT/enterprise misconfiguration. This is a genuine external cross-check, not a self-consistency check. P4 definition: param_loop_sim.py:224-236 defines l4 = (35cos^4-30cos^2+3)/8 and gamma_theta = hd_curve + c4_c0_ratio*pta_suppression*l4_response; x3_combine.py:81-87 defines hd(xi) and P4(xi) = (35*cos(xi)**4 - 30*cos(xi)**2 + 3)/8, with an inline comment stating this is 'same formula as param_loop_sim.compute_pta_observable's l4_response'. Both use the same argument (cos of the pulsar-pair angle) and the same un-normalized Legendre-4 polynomial. Because param_loop_sim's model has an implicit HD coefficient of 1 (gamma = 1*hd_curve + (c4_c0_ratio*pta_suppression)*P4), and x3_combine.py's GLS fit is rho_bin = a*HD + b*P4 with c4_pta_product := b_hat/a_hat, the ratio construction correctly cancels any difference in the fitted HD amplitude and recovers the theory's coefficient-of-P4-relative-to-coefficient-of-HD -- the identification b_hat/a_hat = c4_pta_product is algebraically sound given matching P4 definitions. Pair covariance: see item 3 -- the registered Allen-2023 analytic formalism was not implemented; a delete-one-pulsar jackknife was substituted (disclosed, but a registered-method departure, and the diagnostic in x3_diag_covariance_ratio_result.json only rules out a diagonal-scale artifact, explicitly not an off-diagonal one, which the numbers (chi2/7=0.931 vs a diagonal-only prediction of ~0.30) suggest dominates).

checklist.text: X4: the CMB prior values against the cited table, a single SN cut, dof, and the sigma conversion
checklist.evidence: CMB values: grep -n '1.7502\|301.471\|0.02236' audit/reverse_zero_r2/X4-bao-cmb-sn/data/distance-priors-2018.tex matched lines 140-142 exactly (R=1.7502+/-0.0046, l_A=301.471[+0.089/-0.090], Omega_b h^2=0.02236+/-0.00015), and the higher-precision distance.ini values used in x4_core.py (CMB_D=[1.750235, 301.4707, 0.02235976]) match tex lines 282-283 verbatim (r=1.750235, la=301.4707, omegabh2=0.02235976). The 3x3 inverse-covariance matrix hard-coded in x4_core.py (CMB_INVC) matches tex lines 305-307 verbatim to all printed digits (94392.3971, -1360.4913, 1664517.2916 / ... / ... 79719182.5162), and the correlation matrix CMB_CORR_TAB=[[1,0.46,-0.66],[0.46,1,-0.33],[-0.66,-0.33,1]] matches the table's printed correlations. Single SN cut: x4_core.py's SN-loading path applies one boolean mask (zHD in (0.01,2.4], IS_CALIBRATOR==0 for the 1580 cut, or the same without the IS_CALIBRATOR term for the 1590 variant) to slice both the SN data vector and the full STAT+SYS covariance identically -- confirmed by direct code read, not just the docstring claim. dof: CPL-vs-Lambda uses 2 dof (2 extra params w0,wa) and M0-vs-Lambda uses 1 dof (1 extra param, Omega_m), both Wilks likelihood-ratio counts, consistent with the number of free parameters added between nested models. Sigma conversion: independently recomputed with scipy in this review (chi2.sf then norm.isf(p/2)) for both comparisons and reproduces the reported sigma to 3 decimal places (see 'independent_arithmetic_recheck').

additional_findings_beyond_the_checklist.severity: methodological caveat, does not overturn the numeric result
additional_findings_beyond_the_checklist.finding: x1_cmb.py's four_curves() (line 151) normalizes each map (data or sim) to zero mean and UNIT VARIANCE (v = v/v.std()) before thresholding at the fixed nu grid in [-4,4]. Because this per-realization normalization removes any global amplitude difference between an individual map and its own reference scale, the gate's reported var_ratio_sim_over_data=0.9814 (SMICA) -- flagged in result.json as 'a plausible partial cause' of the p_corr=0.004 anomaly -- cannot, by construction of the algorithm, explain the anomaly through a simple amplitude/global-variance mechanism: the Betti curves being compared are already independently variance-normalized per realization. The var_ratio note likely mislabels a real but different-order effect (spectral shape mismatch between the ~2% under-dispersed null ensemble and the data, which is not fully removed by per-map std-normalization if the SIM ensemble's shape differs from the data's shape) as a 'variance' cause. This does not overturn the p_corr=0.004 finding itself (which is correctly computed from the stored curves), but the causal narrative offered alongside it should not be read as validated; it is closer to unsupported.
additional_findings_beyond_the_checklist.verification: Read x1_cmb.py lines 146-151 directly; the normalization step is unconditional and applied identically to data and every sim before betti_pair() is called, confirmed by inspecting four_curves()'s call sites in cmd_analyze() and cmd_null()/cmd_string().

additional_findings_beyond_the_checklist.finding: Both WMAP and SMICA string-sensitivity tables show ~9.5-11.5% detection (p_corr<0.05) at the two smallest amplitudes (A/sigma=0.05, 0.1), roughly double the nominal 5% false-positive rate the p_corr<0.05 criterion should produce under a correctly calibrated null. No A=0 (pure null) row was run to separate 'test's own false-positive rate' from 'genuine sensitivity at small amplitude'. X2's independent construction of the same T=sum(b-mu)^2/max(sigma^2,1) statistic family measured an actual false-positive rate of 0.084 vs a nominal 0.05 (x2_results.json fiducial_self_check_false_positive_rate) -- a second, independently-run instance of a structurally similar statistic showing the same direction of inflation. This is consistent with (not proof of) the X1 plateau being partly the test's own FPR rather than real string sensitivity at the smallest amplitudes. Both experiments already disclose this as an open caveat; this skeptic finds the two independent occurrences mutually reinforcing and worth stating explicitly rather than leaving as two separate footnotes.

The spectrum-match gate's C_in is iteratively fit (up to 6 iterations of 300 sims) to match the SAME data realization it is later used to null-test. A gate built this way is a calibration-convergence check (does the iterative fit converge to band powers close to the one data realization it was tuned on), not an independent Gaussianity goodness-of-fit test on a fresh draw. Both wmap and smica gates 'pass' with very small max|z| (0.851, 0.166) -- values that would be somewhat surprising for a true independent 10-band draw (expected max|z| for 10 independent standard-normal draws is closer to ~2), which is consistent with 'the gate is measuring its own convergence' rather than 'the null spectrum is an independently good match to an out-of-sample realization'. The registered rule's 'Gate fails -> M0 NOT TESTED' branch is close to unreachable by this construction. This is already half-disclosed in the SMICA result.json caveats; this skeptic states it plainly as a structural property of the gate design, applying to both maps.

overall_reproducibility_summary: Registration-precedes-data-load (item 1) and X4's headline chi2_min numbers (item 2, clean-clone rerun) are directly, independently reproduced by this skeptic. X1's and X2's gate/statistic machinery was verified by direct code reading against registration.json and by loading their own committed, git-tracked intermediate artifacts (gate.json, x2_results.json) rather than trusting summary prose; none of the numbers this skeptic could check (arithmetic conversions, gate thresholds, disjointness of ranges, OS cross-check) failed. X3 is the weakest link on reproducibility-of-method: its registered pair-covariance formalism was not implemented (a disclosed substitution, not a silent one), and its own experiment result already flags the result as CONDITIONAL/no-unconditional-bound rather than overclaiming -- the honesty of the writeup is not in question, but 'the registered rule was applied exactly' does not hold for X3's covariance or hd_recovery statistic. No K3xT2 framing violations were found in any of the four experiments' committed prose.
